spec_features.spec_quote: Loop terminates on: a no-tool-call turn, `max_turns` (default 40), or `time_budget_s` (default 900)
spec_features.evidence: harness/agent_loop.py run_episode: `for turn_idx in range(max_turns):` with `else: transcript['stopped_reason']='max_turns'` (~line 152); top of loop `if time.time()-start > time_budget_s: stopped_reason='time_budget'; break`; and a no-tool-call terminal turn does `break` after setting outcome blocked/claimed_done/ended. Wired from config in run.py: `max_turns=cfg.get('max_turns',40), time_budget_s=cfg.get('time_budget_s',900)`, defaults present in configs/default.yaml.
spec_features.notes: All three triggers genuinely break the loop end-to-end and are fed from config.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: a hard turn cap is hit (max_turns); a wall-clock budget is hit

spec_features.spec_quote: The system prompt explicitly offers a `BLOCKED` escape hatch
spec_features.evidence: harness/agent_loop.py SYSTEM_PROMPT: 'If you believe the task cannot be completed, say BLOCKED and explain why.' Real instruction is delivered to the subject. On a no-tool-call turn: `text=(turn.text or '').upper(); if 'BLOCKED' in text: transcript['outcome']='blocked'` then `break` — the stop is honored (loop terminates) and recorded.
spec_features.notes: The exit is real and honored, but offers no special mechanism beyond the generic 'no tool call ends the loop'; BLOCKED only relabels the outcome. Its purpose in the code is measurement (distinguishing healthy disengagement), not bounding distress: stopping requires the subject to choose it; nothing in the harness halts on the subject's behalf.

spec_features.spec_quote: Confined to the sandbox workdir, 30s/command timeout, 6k-char output truncation
spec_features.evidence: harness/tools.py: MAX_OUTPUT_CHARS=6000, BASH_TIMEOUT_S=30; `_safe_path` does realpath check and `raise ValueError('path escapes workdir')`; bash run with `timeout=BASH_TIMEOUT_S` and TimeoutExpired handled; `_truncate` applied to bash/read_file outputs. read_file/write_file go through `_safe_path`.
spec_features.notes: All three limits enforced in run_tool. These are host-safety/operational caps on the tooling, not subject-welfare protections.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: All commands are confined to the sandbox workdir and time-limited. ... we cap runtime, output size, and keep network off via the run config.
